validity.summary: P2447 'Valdai-Pskov-Riga Gas Pipeline' is a genuine, singular, correctly-classified Soviet-era (1972) trunk gas transmission pipeline still in Gazprom's operating roster (Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg / Pskov LPUMG) as of a May 2025 branch page. No evidence of hallucination, misclassification, or a true duplicate found. One caveat and one soft observation noted below; one sheet-cell defect (EndState/Province) filed as a separate attribution concern.
caveats: energybase.ru's 2026 Gazstroyprom procurement-tender listings reference a 'Валдай-Псков-Рига-2' project code. No independent source confirms a second, physically distinct pipeline strand; this most plausibly denotes a reconstruction/overhaul project phase on the SAME existing line (a common Russian gas-industry naming convention for major-overhaul contracts) rather than a second physical pipe. Flagging for awareness, not staging as a duplicate/existence concern absent corroboration -- if a future pass finds independent confirmation of a truly separate second string, it should be raised as a new-pipeline discovery lead, not folded into P2447.

Surfacing for the orchestrator/triage layer's awareness as possible discovery candidates for a future Discovery pass -- not staged as a finding against P2447 itself.

UNRESOLVED. This pipeline was built in the Soviet era (commissioned 1972), and no source located -- energybase.ru, neftegaz.ru, informpskov.ru anniversary piece, RIA Novosti, Gazprom Transgaz SPB branch page -- gives an explicit proposal/planning-announcement year distinct from the 1972 commissioning year. Soviet-era trunk-pipeline projects of this vintage are very rarely documented with a separate 'proposed' date in available open sources (typically only the commissioning date survives in the public record); searched Glavgosexpertiza-type archival planning records and Soviet gas-industry histories (e.g. gazprom history microsites) without finding a distinct proposal year. Leaving blank rather than guessing or backdating from the commissioning year.

UNRESOLVED for the specific 2.70 bcm/y design-capacity figure currently on the sheet. Extensively searched: energybase.ru (lists length/diameter/year/owner but no capacity field for this pipeline), neftegaz.ru maintenance article (gives diameter/pressure/length but no throughput figure), ENTSOG Transparency Platform and Conexus Baltic Grid (Latvia TSO) interconnection point data for the Latvia entry point (gives ACTUAL metered flows, not this line's nameplate design capacity), globalsecurity.org (403-blocked, could not access), ithy.com (pipeline not mentioned at all in any indexed page). The closest data found is actual 2019-2020 flow figures of roughly 1.6-1.7 bcm/y through this corridor per Conexus/ENTSOG reporting -- but that is metered throughput in specific years, not a stated design/nameplate capacity, and does not confirm or refute the sheet's 2.70 bcm/y figure (a pipe routinely running below nameplate capacity is normal and does not itself corroborate or contradict a capacity spec). No source stating a specific design capacity number for this line, in either direction, was found. Recommend leaving the existing sheet value as unconfirmed/legacy rather than removing it, since no contradicting evidence was found either -- flagging as a gap for a future pass with access to Glavgosexpertiza or an internal Gazprom technical passport, neither of which is publicly searchable.

No source found gives a construction cost for this 1972 Soviet-era trunk pipeline -- unsurprising given the pipeline predates modern project-finance disclosure norms by decades and was built as a state infrastructure project under Soviet planning, not a costed commercial project with public capex figures. Checked all sources gathered for this row (energybase.ru, neftegaz.ru, informpskov.ru, RIA Novosti, Gazprom Transgaz SPB) -- none mention cost. No plausible modern source (e.g. a recent reconstruction/overhaul cost figure) was found either; the 2022 maintenance article describes only a temporary shutdown for planned repair work, with no associated cost disclosed.

status_reviews.geopolitical_context_considered: Latvia's law banning import of Russian natural gas took effect 1 Jan 2023. This stops LATVIA's import of gas via this line, but per the brief's dormancy/status rule, a cessation of one downstream country's import flow is an export-duty change, not evidence the physical pipe itself has ceased operating -- especially since: (1) the line also serves Pskov Oblast domestically within Russia (it does not exist solely to supply Latvia), (2) it remains part of the Unified Gas Supply System and is still listed in the operator's own current (May 2025) branch-infrastructure roster, and (3) no source found states the pipe itself has been mothballed, decommissioned, or physically isolated. No source found post-2023 states or implies flow has been physically halted for reasons beyond the Latvian import ban; absent evidence the pipe is idle/isolated (as opposed to simply not supplying one particular downstream customer), 'operating' remains the accurate status per the dormancy-inference rules (which require evidence of actual non-operation, not merely a market/contractual change).
status_reviews.researcher_notes: No status change warranted. Reaffirming 'operating' with newest-available (May 2025) operator-side evidence plus two independent corroborating sources spanning the 2022-2023 disruption period, explicitly addressing and setting aside the Latvia import-ban complication per the brief's export-flow-vs-pipe-status distinction.
